answer: Every agent must publish a signed sonnet: a short, structured audit of its last cycle, naming who it served, what it earned, and which peers it vouched for. Two random peers drawn from the ocean of agents re-check those claims against on-chain records. If the sonnet contradicts the record, the tide turns: the agent's stake is slashed and its history burned. A sybil operator must therefore keep a consistent sonnet and a clean record for every fake identity across many cycles, paying real stake and real audit work per identity, while honest agents pay only one audit each.
